root_idea.summary: The root denotes shaking, trembling, and movement, especially movement that is unstable, convulsive, or repeatedly agitated.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of shaking extends to directed head gestures, trembling teeth, moving clouds, anatomical parts characterized by mobility, and names for animals marked by such movement.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form IV verb is presented under its normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form, أَنْغَضَ.

senses.definition: To shake or wag the head toward someone, as a gesture of astonishment, disapproval, or derision.
senses.usage_conditions: In the attested Quranic construction, the head is the object of the motion and the movement is directed toward an addressee with إِلَى. The gesture may express wonder, disapproval, mockery, or a questioning response.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move in a shaking, tremulous, convulsive, or unstable manner; to shake, wobble, totter, wag, or nod.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a head, a camel’s saddle, a tooth, or other things; it can also describe a person becoming agitated or disquieted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rise, hasten, and go forth toward an enemy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic or figurative use describing movement toward an enemy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dense or abundant; of a cloud, to become dense or rain-ready and to move or travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions of the cloud vary between internal billowing or movement of one part into another and movement along; the lexical branch concerns cloud density and movement associated with rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an affair or case, to become weak or unsound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to the condition of an affair or matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a thing into a state of motion or agitation; to shake, wag, wobble, totter, or nod it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use, said of a thing or of the head. The directed head gesture attested in the Quran is listed separately above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who shakes the head and trembles in gait.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An inflectional noun used as an epithet.
The name is associated with the bird’s repeated head movement when hastening or, in some descriptions, with its habit of going around.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel with a large hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the shaking or quaking of a large hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Much or intensely shaking, wagging, nodding, or agitated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive adjective; it can describe camels that jog greatly with their saddles or make their saddles jolt repeatedly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wrinkled or ridged in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression or epithet applied to a person; the source also reports an alternative derivation involving transposition from a word for wrinkles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moving, agitated, or shaking; of a cloud, becoming dense and rain-ready while its parts billow or move into one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cloud may be described as moving internally without traveling along, although some accounts allow movement or travel more generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cartilage of the shoulder blade, especially a part that moves to and fro; also the base of the neck where the head moves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical use covering the mobile part or extremity of the shoulder-blade cartilage and the corresponding neck region.
